subject: Logic
title: Eratosthenes Measures Earth
description: A short lesson to help you apply Eratosthenes Measures Earth.

hook.text: In 240 BC, a man in Egypt measured the entire planet with a stick, a shadow, and a walk between two cities.

buildup.text: Eratosthenes noticed the sun cast no shadow in Syene at noon but cast one at 7.2° in Alexandria, 800 km north.

discovery.text: 7.2° is 1/50 of a full circle. So Earth's circumference is roughly 50 × 800 km = 40,000 km. Astonishingly accurate.

twist.text: He assumed Earth was a sphere and sunlight arrived parallel—both brilliant assumptions validated by the result.

climax.text: The power of the proof isn't the answer—it's that simple geometry and clear logic measured the immeasurable.

punchline.text: A stick and a shadow measured the world.

quiz.question: How did Eratosthenes measure Earth's circumference?
options: Using shadow angles between two cities and geometry
